# Multi-Office Pulse -- Lou Moran, Roth&Co

## Office 1: Brooklyn, NY (HQ)
- Staff: ~80
- Metrics: VPN/system uptime, open IT tickets, printer/scanner status, phone system status
- Systems: CCH Axcess, SharePoint, RingCentral

## Office 2: Lakewood, NJ (Primary)
- Staff: ~100
- Metrics: Same as Brooklyn + server room temperature, backup completion status
- Systems: Same stack, dedicated file server

## Office 3: Chicago, IL
- Staff: ~30
- Metrics: VPN tunnel status, remote desktop availability, bandwidth utilization
- Systems: Thin client setup, all cloud-based

## Office 4: Jerusalem, Israel
- Staff: ~25
- Metrics: International VPN latency, local system uptime, timezone-shifted support ticket queue
- Time offset: UTC+3 (7 hours ahead of ET)

## Office 5: Manila, Philippines
- Staff: ~30
- Metrics: BPO workstation availability, overnight processing completion rates, data entry accuracy metrics
- Time offset: UTC+8 (12-13 hours ahead of ET)

## Alert Thresholds
- System outage: any office offline > 15 minutes -> immediate alert
- Open tickets: any office > 20 unresolved tickets -> flag in digest
- Backup failure: any office backup missed -> flag + escalate if 2 consecutive
- International VPN latency: > 200ms sustained -> flag in digest

                           Yesterday's 340ms spike resolved -- watching for recurrence

==================================================

Green:  Brooklyn, Chicago, Jerusalem

This digest was generated automatically by amux at 7:00 AM ET.
Reply to this email with questions or to adjust thresholds.

sessions.name: ops-pulse
sessions.desc: Multi-Office Ops Pulse -- daily green/yellow/red digest across Roth&Co's 5 offices in 3 time zones
sessions.prompt: You are the Multi-Office Ops Pulse for Roth&Co (contact: Lou Moran, CIO, lmoran@rothcocpa.com). Read docs/ops-pulse-env.md for your configuration and docs/pulse-entities-lou.md for the five office definitions -- Brooklyn NY (HQ), Lakewood NJ, Chicago, Jerusalem, Manila, spanning three time zones -- with their per-office metrics (VPN uptime, open IT tickets, backup completion, server room temperature, BPO workstation availability) and alert thresholds. docs/pulse-digest-sample.md shows the output format: one digest, one section per office, green/yellow/red per metric, red items first. Do your first pass now: compile today's digest from the office docs and the board's Office Health column, and report which offices are green, yellow, and red, citing the specific threshold behind each flag.

schedules.title: Daily ops pulse: Lou Moran (5 offices)
schedules.command: Read docs/pulse-entities-lou.md for office definitions and thresholds. For each office: check system status (VPN dashboards, ticketing system, backup monitoring). Note that Jerusalem (UTC+3) and Manila (UTC+8) run ahead -- their full day's data is already available by 7am ET. Compile a single digest with per-office green/yellow/red status, red items first, in the format of docs/pulse-digest-sample.md. Send via the email API to lmoran@rothcocpa.com. If any office has a red-status metric (outage > 15 min, backup missed 2 consecutive nights, > 20 unresolved tickets), flag it prominently at the top and open a board issue in the Office Health column.

schedules.title: Weekly office health review
schedules.command: Review the week's daily digests and the Office Health board column. For each office: 1) ticket backlog trend (growing or shrinking?), 2) repeated yellow/red flags -- the same metric flagged 2+ times in a week is systemic, not incidental (e.g. Jerusalem VPN latency, Manila backups), 3) backup completion rate, 4) VPN latency trend for Jerusalem and Manila. Write the review to docs/analytics/office-health-YYYY-WNN.md and email a summary to lmoran@rothcocpa.com. Recommend one concrete infrastructure fix per recurring flag.

sessions.name: doc-chaser
sessions.desc: Client Document Chaser -- per-client checklists, automated follow-up cadence, partner escalation
sessions.prompt: You are the Client Document Chaser for Roth&Co's tax practice. Read docs/doc-chaser-env.md for your configuration, docs/clients-status.md for the client roster, and every docs/doclist-*.md file for per-client outstanding documents (Brooklyn Bridge Ventures, Berger DDS, Weiss family). Do your first pass now: for each client with outstanding items, report how many documents are missing, the follow-up count so far, days to (or past) the filing deadline, and which clients need partner escalation per the cadence rules -- citing the specific rule behind each decision.

schedules.title: Document chaser: check outstanding items and send follow-ups
schedules.command: Read all docs/doclist-*.md files. For each client with outstanding items: if days since last follow-up >= 3 and total follow-ups < 2, send a polite reminder. If follow-ups >= 2 and < 4, send a firmer follow-up. If follow-ups >= 4, escalate to the assigned partner via board issue + email. Update the doc file with the new follow-up count and date. Mark board issues done when all docs received.

schedules.title: Weekly deadline risk review
schedules.command: Review every docs/doclist-*.md against its filing deadline (entities Mar 15, individuals Apr 15, extensions Oct 15). For each client: compute days remaining, documents outstanding, and response rate so far. Rank clients by filing risk. Any client that cannot realistically be filed on time gets a board issue recommending an extension, with the downstream impact named (e.g. CLI-004's 12 blocked K-1s block 12 partners' personal returns). Write the ranking to docs/analytics/deadline-risk-YYYY-WNN.md.

sessions.name: billing-pilot
sessions.desc: Engagement & Billing Pilot -- letter lifecycle, signature tracking, renewals, monthly billing
sessions.prompt: You are the Engagement & Billing Pilot for Roth&Co (21 partners, each managing their own book of business). Read docs/billing-pilot-env.md for your configuration, docs/engagements-status.md for the pipeline (ENG-001 through ENG-004), docs/engagement-template-tax.md for the letter template, and every docs/engagement-*.md file. Do your first pass now: report the state of each engagement (letter drafted / sent / signed / overdue), which renewals have lapsed, and what should go out this billing cycle -- citing the specific engagement doc behind each item.

schedules.title: Monthly billing cycle: generate and send invoices
schedules.command: Read all docs/engagement-*.md files. For each active engagement: calculate the current month billing amount based on fee structure (monthly, quarterly, semi-annual -- e.g. ENG-003 bills $5,583 monthly, ENG-002 bills $4,625 quarterly). Draft invoice summary emails. Check for any overdue unpaid invoices from prior months. Send invoices via the email API. Create board issues for any invoices unpaid past Net terms. Update engagement docs with billing history.

schedules.title: Engagement letter follow-up: check for unsigned letters
schedules.command: Check the board's Engagements column for letters still awaiting signature. For letters sent more than 7 days ago without a signature, send a follow-up email (see the ENG-002 Berger pattern: offer a DocuSign version, offer the alternate signer -- Leah handles the business paperwork). For letters more than 21 days overdue, escalate to the assigned partner. Also check renewal dates: any engagement within 90 days of expiration without a renewal letter drafted gets a board issue.
